messages:
sophia_ml: Quick update from the per-channel rescale runs on the AWQ vs GPTQ bakeoff. Ran MMLU/HellaSwag/PIQA sweep with our new detector + adaptive-skip policy. Results are weird — some channels show huge sigma spikes but overall FLOP cost drops ~22%.

ajay: Can you paste the detector output? especially the per-channel stats for the outlier window.

sophia_ml: Paste below. flagged channels are the ones exceeding 6 sigma in any 128-token window.

```
> eval snapshot: awq-per-channel-2026-03-18
channel 19: max 0.8 sigma
channel 237: max 11.2 sigma -> FLAG (rare big outliers)
channel 401: max 6.3 sigma -> borderline
channel 512: max 1.1 sigma
channel 1024: max 0.9 sigma
channels flagged count: 7/4096
mean delta (AWQ vs FP16) on MMLU: -0.9% absolute
p95 latency drop: 18%
cost per token: -22%
```

marco_research: Interesting — 7 channels flagged but delta small. That suggests outliers are very sparse but high magnitude. Did you try hybrid repair (FP16 just for flagged channels)?

sophia_ml: Yes, quick hybrid: fallback flagged channels to FP16 during inference (merge kernel). Accuracy recovered to -0.2% and latency penalty ~+4% vs pure AWQ. Still much cheaper than GPTQ baseline.

riley_prod: That hybrid approach sounds promising for Dedicated profile where we can trade a bit of latency for quality. Any stability regressions across prompts?

sophia_ml: Ran 300 prompt long-tail pass (logs attached in the eval job). No systematic fail modes, but a couple of code-gen prompts had token hallucination shifts — both tied to channel 237 and 401.

ajay: Could we try an adaptive rescale instead of full FP16 fallback? e.g., per-channel multiplier alpha = clip(1 / (1 + sigma_window), 0.5, 2.0) applied during quantization stage, then re-eval. That might reduce the latency hit.

marco_research: Agreed. I sketched a quick patch:
```
# pseudo
for c in channels:
    s = sigma[c]
    alpha = max(0.5, min(2.0, 1.0 / (1 + s)))
    Wq[:,c] *= alpha
```
Run it with `--per-channel-rescale adaptive` flag.

sophia_ml: Kicked a job: `python eval.py --model awq-14b --quant awq --per-channel-rescale adaptive --window 128 --hybrid-threshold 8.0`

deploy-bot: deploy event: canary eval job awq-per-channel-adaptive-177399 queued by sophia_ml (job id j-9983).

ops_jules: FYI if this reduces latency variance we can push a canary on Dedicated 1 node pool. Want me to reserve?

riley_prod: Please reserve a node pool and attach token-level tracing. If hybrid fallback happens >1% of tokens, abort canary.

ajay: Also minimal ask: log per-channel repair counts and average alpha applied, we need that for Optimize recommendations.

sophia_ml: Will add those logs. Expect results in ~45m, I'll post the summary. :hourglass:

marco_research: Small note — try the same adaptive rescale but with window=64 and windowed clipping; I suspect the outliers are short bursts and smaller window picks them up more precisely.

sophia_ml: Good call, I'll run window=64 as a follow-up if current job shows mixed signals.

riley_prod: Nice work — this pathway (detect -> adaptive rescale -> hybrid fallback) could be a standard onboarding recipe for new models. Let's document it in the onboarding checklist if it stabilizes. :white_check_mark:
